The change that made the configured value take effect is the O3-6028 fix, which passes `chooseLocation.locationsPerRequest` into the login location picker and removes the unused `chooseLocation.numberToShow` property. The line that passes it to the picker is `openmrs-esm-core/packages/apps/esm-login-app/src/location-picker/location-picker-view.component.tsx:181`, where it is wrapped in `Math.max(..., 1)`.

The 50 default comes from the picker itself: `LocationPicker` defaults `locationsPerRequest` to 50 when none is passed, so any caller that omits the prop gets 50. The login app's config schema defaults the setting to 50 as well, so an implementation that configures nothing still gets 50.

I could not find the commit SHA for the change. Falkon's grep returned no commit metadata, and I have no history tool in this session. The changeset file is the only record I found, so the ticket and changeset are the anchors for the fix.

Evidence, best first:

1. `openmrs-esm-core/.changeset/login-locations-per-request.md:5` describes the fix: it passes `chooseLocation.locationsPerRequest` to the picker and removes `numberToShow`.
2. `openmrs-esm-core/packages/apps/esm-login-app/src/location-picker/location-picker-view.component.tsx:181` is the line that passes the configured value to `LocationPicker`.
3. `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-styleguide/src/location-picker/location-picker.component.tsx:27` is the `locationsPerRequest = 50` default that applied when nothing was passed.
4. `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-styleguide/src/location-picker/location-picker.component.tsx:42` passes `locationsPerRequest` into `useLocations`, which is where the page size takes effect.
5. `openmrs-esm-core/packages/apps/esm-login-app/src/config-schema.ts:44-49` defines the `locationsPerRequest` config property with a default of 50 and a greater-than-zero validator.
6. `openmrs-esm-core/packages/apps/esm-login-app/src/location-picker/location-picker.test.tsx:435-457` tests that the configured value reaches the picker and that zero falls back to 1.
